Server-side document layout contract: GenerateLayoutSnapshotJson lays out a DocumentEditorDocument with the SAME JavaScript layout chain the canvas editor paints with (the embedded headless bundle) and returns the schema v1 layout snapshot JSON — the exact contract of DocumentPdfExportRequest.LayoutSnapshotJson, consumable by TempoDocumentPdfRenderer for WYSIWYG-parity PDF output without a browser. Accepts an optional page-setup override (size/orientation/margins in points), the font faces the PDF renderer embeds (required — layout fails closed without them), and a tracked-changes display mode for redline printing. Implementations are engine-hosting details (JintDocumentLayoutEngine today, swappable for another JS host or a native port without touching consumers); register via AddTempoDocumentLayout().

Headless document rendering facade: one call takes a template (or plain document) plus token values and produces a WYSIWYG PDF (RenderPdfAsync = DocumentAssemblyService.Assemble → ITempoDocumentLayoutService → TempoDocumentPdfRenderer, incl. watermark and forensic watermark passthrough) or per-page PNG previews at a parametrizable DPI (RenderPageImagesAsync — visual feedback for agents, tests and preview tooling). Register via AddTempoDocumentServices().

ITempoDocumentLayoutService hosted in Jint: evaluates the embedded headless layout bundle once per pooled engine and calls its generateHeadlessLayoutSnapshotJson seam — one JSON request in (canvas model + Skia advance tables), one JSON result out, no .NET↔JS callbacks per glyph. Engines are pooled thread-safely and bounded by observed concurrency, so repeated MCP/preview traffic never allocates an engine per call (CreatedEngineCount exposes pooling diagnostics). Fail-closed: missing fonts, an unknown font family, an unmeasurable glyph, or a JS failure throw TempoDocumentLayoutException with diagnostics instead of degrading the layout silently. Measured 2026-07-19 (Jint 4.13, .NET 10, Debug): ≈2.2 s cold / ≈0.9 s warm for a 54-page document (≈17 ms/page warm).

items.description: Access to the embedded headless document layout bundle — the canvas editor's layout chain (layout snapshot export → display list → pagination → line breaker/paragraph engine/font metrics) compiled into a single ESM artifact by scripts/build-document-editor.mjs (npm run build:document-editor). Server-side layout hosts evaluate this script to produce the exact layout snapshot the browser editor exports, giving WYSIWYG parity by construction without a C# port of the layout code. Text measurement is injectable: pass a { measureRun } partial as options.fontMetrics, or create a service via createFontMetricsService — without a canvas context it falls back to deterministic synthetic metrics.

items.description: An image reference the headless pipeline needs an embeddable source for: the owning document id, the provider asset id (when asset-backed) and the original URL (never an already-embeddable data URI). Passed to TempoDocumentImageSourceResolver before layout.

Fail-closed headless layout error: thrown when a layout could not be produced with WYSIWYG parity — no fonts were provided, the document references font families the provided faces cannot resolve (UnknownFontFamilies), glyphs are missing from resolved faces (MissingGlyphs), or the JS engine failed. Carries the measurement diagnostics so callers can report exactly which font faces to provide.

Diagnostic record for a glyph the provided font faces cannot measure: the resolved font family whose advance table lacks the glyph and the Unicode code point of the unmeasurable character. Reported by TempoDocumentLayoutException.MissingGlyphs.

DI registration for the headless document layout service: AddTempoDocumentLayout() registers ITempoDocumentLayoutService backed by the pooled Jint host (JintDocumentLayoutEngine) as an idempotent singleton.
One rendered page preview from ITempoDocumentService.RenderPageImagesAsync: zero-based page index, raster dimensions in pixels and the PNG bytes.

Result of a headless PDF render: the PDF bytes, the laid-out page count, the layout snapshot JSON (schema v1) the PDF was rendered from — reusable for previews or diagnostics — and the forensic watermark timestamp actually stamped into the PDF when a forensic watermark was requested.

Request for the headless document facade: the template or plain document, optional token values for assembly (null renders the document as-is), export options (page setup, review display mode, watermark, forensic watermark), the font faces to measure and embed with (required for WYSIWYG-accurate output) and optional document id / file name.

Default ITempoDocumentService: composes the server-side document pipeline — document assembly (IF/ELSE conditional chains, repeating sections, computed expressions over token values), headless canvas layout (pooled Jint host) and Skia PDF/raster rendering with embedded fonts. The clock is injectable via TimeProvider, so assembly date functions (TODAY/DATEADD) and the forensic watermark timestamp are deterministic under test; a missing forensic timestamp is stamped from the injected clock rather than an uncontrolled UtcNow. RenderPdfAsync returns the PDF plus page count and the layout snapshot JSON it was rendered from; RenderPageImagesAsync rasters every page to PNG at the requested DPI (96 = CSS pixel scale).

DI registration for the headless document facade: AddTempoDocumentServices() registers the full pipeline — ITempoDocumentLayoutService (pooled Jint host) and the ITempoDocumentService facade (assembly → layout → PDF / PNG previews) — as idempotent singletons; the facade resolves a registered TimeProvider when present, otherwise uses the system clock.

Precomputed glyph metrics for one font face in font design units (unhinted, linear): Unicode-keyed advance widths, ascent/descent/line gap, units-per-em and the missing-glyph advance. Produced by TempoFontAdvanceTableExtractor from the same TTF/OTF bytes the PDF renderer embeds; code points the font has no glyph for are omitted so the JS measurer can fall back to synthetic metrics with diagnostics.

Extracts glyph advance tables and vertical metrics from ReportPdfFontFace bytes via SkiaSharp (SKTypeface/SKFont with unhinted linear metrics at font-unit scale) and serializes them into the compact JSON the headless JS layout bundle measures with (createAdvanceFontMetricsService). Because the tables come from the SAME font bytes the PDF renderer embeds, headless measurement and PDF drawing agree by construction — no .NET↔JS callbacks per glyph. Default coverage: Basic Latin, Latin-1, Latin Extended-A/B (Czech and Central European diacritics), general punctuation and the euro sign; extendable via additionalCodePoints. Extraction is cached per face (family, weight, style, content hash) behind a thread-safe lazy cache; use the Shared instance for process-wide reuse.

Server-side image resolution seam for the headless facade (TempoDocumentRenderRequest.ImageResolver): resolves an image reference (asset id / URL) to an embeddable data URI before layout, so headless exports embed real images — the counterpart of the browser's IDocumentImageUrlResolver. Return null to leave the reference unresolved; its footprint then renders as a placeholder rectangle. Hosts should prefer asset-backed images for server-rendered exports; host-relative URLs are not resolvable on the server.

Production PDF renderer for TmDocumentEditor exports. Consumes the canonical document plus the canvas layout snapshot (DocumentPdfExportRequest.LayoutSnapshotJson, schema v1) captured by the editor, translates the exact painted primitives into the Skia PDF backend, and emits a vector PDF with a searchable text layer and embedded, subset fonts — inheriting the editor's line and page breaking for WYSIWYG parity.

Options for TempoDocumentPdfRenderer: font faces (family, weight, style, bytes) available for deterministic embedded rendering with subsetting, and the fallback font family used when a text command carries none.

Exports a DocumentCompareResult as a redline DOCX: builds the tracked-changes document via DocumentRedlineBuilder and writes it with the standard DOCX exporter, whose revision support emits real w:ins/w:del elements with author and date — Word and the DOCX importer see reviewable tracked changes.
